description: Does a returning visitor's browser reuse compiled engine code? September 13, 2026, leviathan CPUs 88-91, Chromium 151.0.7922.137, site at cdb3bdd (engine-20260913-1524). One record per visit; visits of one sample share a browser profile. Variants: shim-600 (no COOP/COEP from the server so coi-serviceworker activates, Cache-Control max-age=600: GitHub Pages today), real-600 (real headers, max-age=600), real-immut (real headers, max-age=31536000 immutable: Cloudflare Pages with site/_headers), real-reval and real-etag (max-age=0, every visit revalidates and gets a 304), nostore (Cache-Control: no-store, the tools/cpu-test.py server), shim-skip (shim active, patched to leave the same-origin .wasm fetch alone). trace.counts holds V8's v8.wasm trace event counts for the visit: wasm.Deserialize > 0 means the code cache was read, wasm.SerializeModule means it was written. perf_at_shell.turbofan is the number of engine functions the V8 perf map lists as TurboFan code at the guest prompt. visit_meta.cpu_at_shell is browser process-group CPU from launch to the prompt. shim-skip records came from the agent's hand-patched site; shim-skip-nixbuild from the site as nix/site.nix now builds it.
